before.title: Distinct exponential characters are linearly independent on a nonempty open set, and the real-part grouping rule
before.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set, let $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in\mathbb R^n$ ($m\ge1$) be pairwise distinct, and let $c_1,\dots,c_m\in\mathbb C^q$ for some $q\ge1$ (the scalar case $q=1$ included; all statements below are componentwise). Write $\lambda_j\cdot z$ for the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] on $\mathbb R^n$ and $e^{iw}$ for the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] at $iw$, and consider the $\mathbb C^q$-valued map $F(z):=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\,e^{i\lambda_j\cdot z}$ on $U$. Then: (a) [Complex independence] if $F(z)=0$ for every $z\in U$, then $c_1=\dots=c_m=0$. (b) [Real-part grouping rule] if $\operatorname{Re}F(z)=0$ for every $z\in U$, then for every $
u\in\mathbb R^n$ the grouped coefficient $$C_
u:=\sum_{\lambda_j=
u} c_j+\sum_{\lambda_j=-
u}\overline{c_j}$$ vanishes; in particular $c_j=0$ whenever $\lambda_j
otin\{\lambda_k,-\lambda_k:k
e j\}$. (c) [Scope] no hypothesis beyond pairwise distinctness of the $\lambda_j$ and nonemptiness and openness of $U$ is used; $\lambda_j=0$ is allowed and the $\lambda_j$ need not be nonzero, ordered or normalized. The statement concerns the open set $U$ and asserts nothing on sets with empty interior, where distinct characters can agree.
before.strategy:
Both parts are proved by induction on the dimension $n$; write $z=(z_1,z')$ with $z_1\in\mathbb R$, $z'\in\mathbb R^{n-1}$. Base case $n=1$: let $f(t)=\sum_j c_j e^{i\lambda_jt}$ (with $\lambda_j\in\mathbb R$ distinct) vanish on the nonempty open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R$. Fix $j_0$ and consider the constant-coefficient operator $L:=\prod_{j
e j_0} igl(	frac{d}{dt}-i\lambda_j igr)$. For a single exponential the chain rule and entire-ness of the exponential give $ igl(	frac{d}{dt}-i\lambda igr)e^{i\lambda't}=i(\lambda'-\lambda)e^{i\lambda't}$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[def-complex-exponential]]); differentiating a finite linear combination term by term is the sum rule of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], applied once per factor of $L$. Hence $Lf=\sum_j c_j igl[\prod_{j'
e j_0}i(\lambda_j-\lambda_{j'}) igr]e^{i\lambda_jt}$, and every summand with $j
e j_0$ vanishes because one factor is zero; therefore $Lf=c_{j_0} igl[\prod_{j
e j_0}i(\lambda_{j_0}-\lambda_j) igr]e^{i\lambda_{j_0}t}$. Since $f=0$ on $U$, all derivatives of $f$ vanish on $U$ and so $Lf=0$ on $U$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the product $\prod_{j
e j_0}i(\lambda_{j_0}-\lambda_j)$ is a nonzero complex number (distinct frequencies, [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]], [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]) and $e^{i\lambda_{j_0}t}
e0$, so $c_{j_0}=0$; $j_0$ was arbitrary. Inductive step: assume the statement for $n-1$. Group the indices by the first coordinate: for each value $\mu$ of the $\lambda_{j,1}$ put $P_\mu(z'):=\sum_{\lambda_{j,1}=\mu}c_j\,e^{i\lambda_j'\cdot z'}$, where $\lambda_j'=(\lambda_{j,2},\dots,\lambda_{j,n})\in\mathbb R^{n-1}$; then $F(z_1,z')=\sum_\mu e^{i\mu z_1}P_\mu(z')$. Fix $(z_1^0,z'^0)\in U$; by openness, for all $z'$ in some neighbourhood $V$ of $z'^0$ the set $\{z_1:(z_1,z')\in U\}$ contains an open interval about $z_1^0$, on which the one-variable function $z_1\mapsto F(z_1,z')$ vanishes; the base-case argument applied to its distinct frequencies $\mu$ gives $P_\mu(z')=0$ for every $\mu$ and every $z'\in V$. Each $P_\mu$ is a finite combination of the characters $z'\mapsto e^{i\lambda_j'\cdot z'}$ with pairwise distinct frequencies $\lambda_j'$ (the $\lambda_j$ with first coordinate $\mu$ are pairwise distinct, hence so are their tails), so the induction hypothesis applied on the nonempty open set $V$ gives $c_j=0$ for all $j$ with $\lambda_{j,1}=\mu$; varying $\mu$ gives all $c_j=0$, proving (a). Part (b): the identity $2\operatorname{Re}z=z+\overline z$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]) gives, on $U$, $0=\sum_j c_j e^{i\lambda_j\cdot z}+\sum_j\overline{c_j}e^{-i\lambda_j\cdot z}$; this is a finite $\mathbb C^q$-valued linear combination of characters whose frequencies range over the distinct elements of $\{\lambda_j\}\cup\{-\lambda_j\}$, and the coefficient of the frequency $
u$ after grouping is exactly $C_
u$. Part (a) forces every grouped coefficient to vanish; if $\lambda_j
otin\{\lambda_k,-\lambda_k:k
e j\}$ then $C_{\lambda_j}=c_j$. No choice principle is used. ∎

references.locator: Theorem 1 and its inductive proof (divide by one exponential and differentiate, one frequency at a time): distinct exponentials $e^{\lambda_1 z},\dots,e^{\lambda_m z}$ are linearly independent on the plane. references.title: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory (v5.10), Theorem 5.14 (Dedekind)
references.locator: Theorem 5.14 with proof, printed pp. 85-86: every finite set of distinct group homomorphisms $G\to F^{\times}$ is linearly independent. Read directly in the fetched PDF; for the group $(\mathbb R^n,+)$ the maps $z\mapsto e^{i\lambda\cdot z}$ are distinct characters, so the theorem is the everywhere-vanishing case of clause (a), while the item's induction supplies the localization from a nonempty open set and the real-part grouping of clause (b).

u$. At a self-paired frequency $
u=-\overline
u$, that coefficient is $2\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\lambda_j=
u}c_j$, not the coefficient itself. In particular at zero frequency a purely imaginary coefficient is allowed. before.title: The two-equation interface admittance system: solution formulas and the normal-flux identity
before.statement:
Let $Y_1,Y_2\in\mathbb C$ with $Y_1+Y_2
e0$, and let $E_i,E_r,E_t\in\mathbb C$ satisfy the two linear equations $$E_i+E_r=E_t,\qquad Y_1(E_i-E_r)=Y_2E_t.$$ Then: (a) [Solution] If $E_i
e0$, then $$r:= rac{E_r}{E_i}= rac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t:= rac{E_t}{E_i}= rac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ if $E_i=0$ then $E_r=E_t=0$ and the ratios are undefined. (b) [Normal-flux identity] If $Y_1>0$ is real (the incident side admittance), then $$|r|^2+ rac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^2=1,$$ and explicitly $|t|^2=\dfrac{4Y_1^2}{|Y_1+Y_2|^2}$ and $|r|^2=1-\dfrac{4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{|Y_1+Y_2|^2}$. The second summand $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2$ is nonnegative if and only if $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\ge0$; it is the normal-flux coefficient of a passive transmitted medium and may be negative for an active one, in which case $|r|>1$ and the identity carries no energy-conservation reading. (c) [Pure-imaginary admittance] If $Y_1>0$ is real and $Y_2$ is purely imaginary, then $|r|=1$, $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\,|t|^2=0$ and $|t|^2=\dfrac{4Y_1^2}{Y_1^2+|Y_2|^2}>0$; in particular $r
e0$ and $t
e0$. (d) [Real-positive specialisation] If $Y_1,Y_2>0$ are real, then $r=(Y_1-Y_2)/(Y_1+Y_2)$ and $t=2Y_1/(Y_1+Y_2)$ are real and $|r|^2+(Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2=1$; with $Y_j=1/Z_j$, $Z_j>0$, this is $r=(Z_2-Z_1)/(Z_1+Z_2)$, $t=2Z_2/(Z_1+Z_2)$ and $R+T=1$ for $R=|r|^2$, $T=(Z_1/Z_2)|t|^2$, in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]. (e) [Scope] The lemma is pure algebra of $\mathbb C$; the labels 'incident', 'reflected' and 'transmitted' and the interpretation of the second summand as a flux fraction belong to the consuming physical theorem, not to this lemma.
before.strategy:
Part (a): substitute $E_r=E_t-E_i$ (from the first equation) into the second: $Y_1(2E_i-E_t)=Y_2E_t$, i.e. $2Y_1E_i=(Y_1+Y_2)E_t$; since $Y_1+Y_2
e0$ this gives $E_t=2Y_1E_i/(Y_1+Y_2)$, and then $E_r=E_t-E_i=(Y_1-Y_2)E_i/(Y_1+Y_2)$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]], field arithmetic [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]). If $E_i
e0$ the two ratios are the displayed $r$ and $t$; if $E_i=0$ both $E_r$ and $E_t$ vanish and no ratio is defined. Part (b): use $|z|^2=z\overline z$ and the binomial identity $|Y_1+Y_2|^2-|Y_1-Y_2|^2=4\operatorname{Re}(Y_1\overline{Y_2})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]): for real $Y_1>0$ the right side is $4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2$, so $|r|^2=|Y_1-Y_2|^2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2=1-4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2$ while $|t|^2=4Y_1^2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2$; adding $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2$ cancels the correction term and yields the asserted identity. The sign and active-medium remarks follow from $|r|^2\ge0$ and $|r|>1\iff\operatorname{Re}Y_2<0$ whenever $|t|>0$. Part (c): for $Y_2=i eta$, $ eta\in\mathbb R$, and real $Y_1>0$ one has $\overline{Y_1+Y_2}=Y_1-Y_2$, hence $|r|=|Y_1-Y_2|/|Y_1+Y_2|=1$, and the identity of (b) gives $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\,|t|^2=0$; moreover $Y_1+Y_2
e0$ because $Y_1>0$, so $|t|^2=4Y_1^2/(Y_1^2+ eta^2)>0$. Part (d): substituting $Y_j=1/Z_j$ with $Z_j>0$ into (a) gives $r=(1/Z_1-1/Z_2)/(1/Z_1+1/Z_2)=(Z_2-Z_1)/(Z_1+Z_2)$ and $t=2Z_2/(Z_1+Z_2)$, and (b) gives $|r|^2+(Z_1/Z_2)|t|^2=1$, i.e. $R+T=1$ for the stated $R,T$. All divisions are by nonzero complex numbers; no choice principle is used. ∎

before.title: Plane-wave fields in a homogeneous Ohmic medium: amplitude conditions, dispersion, averaged flux and the evanescent branch
before.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K8 (admittance and flux ingredients); scaffold-added necessary prerequisite (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-34.notes.md)
before.statement:
Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] in its isotropic scalar case at rest in the laboratory frame, with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma\ge0$, the constitutive relations $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], the macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], the fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and the parameters and phase convention of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Consider a declared region with vanishing free charge density and no external free current, so that $ho_f=0$ and the free current is the conduction current $J_f=\sigma E$. Let $k\in\mathbb C^{3}$, $\omega>0$ and $e,h\in\mathbb C^{3}$, and for $(x,t)\in\mathbb R^{3}	imes\mathbb R$ define $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re} igl(e\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)} igr)$ and $H(x,t):=\operatorname{Re} igl(h\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)} igr)$ componentwise, i.e. with the phase convention $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ and the real-part encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]; put $D:=\varepsilon E$, $B:=\mu H$ and $J_f:=\sigma E$. Extend the Euclidean inner and cross products to $\mathbb C^{3}$ by the same componentwise polynomial formulas ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). before.physical_scope: Exact conditional statement about ideal plane-wave fields in a homogeneous isotropic Ohmic medium at rest, on the laboratory chart: the four macroscopic equations hold if and only if the four complex amplitude conditions hold, with the dispersion relation, transverse structure, lossless period-averaged energy density and flux, and the evanescent decay and normal-flux identities. Excluded: bounded or finite-energy fields, interfaces, anisotropic or dispersive media, nonlinear response, ideal conductors, any completeness of the plane-wave family, and all empirical statements.

before.statement:

e0$ then $k_i,k_r,k_t$ all lie in the complex two-dimensional subspace $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{\kappa_i,n\}$ (a real plane when the wavevectors are real); if $\kappa_i=0$ then all three wavevectors are parallel to $n$. e0$ together with $k_j\cdot k_j
e0$; the two normal identities are recorded because they belong to the interface model, but they are not used. after.strategy: On the interface use the six-component tangential trace coefficient $A_j:=(e_j^{\tau},h_j^{\tau})$ and the complex frequency $\lambda_j=(\kappa_j,-\omega_j)\in\mathbb C^3$. Every actual nonzero wave has $A_j\ne0$: if both tangential parts vanished, $e_j=an$ and $h_j=bn$; $k_j\times e_j=\omega_j\mu_jh_j$ equates a tangential vector with a normal one, hence $h_j=0$, and $k_j\times h_j=-\omega_j\varepsilon_je_j$ then forces $e_j=0$. The two tangential boundary identities give $\operatorname{Re}(A_ie^{i\lambda_i\cdot z}+A_re^{i\lambda_r\cdot z}-A_te^{i\lambda_t\cdot z})=0$ on the open real set $\mathbb R^2\times I$. Apply [[lem-em-exponential-character-open-set-independence]](b), which permits complex spatial frequencies. The negative-conjugate partner of each $\lambda_j$ has positive last coordinate $+\omega_j$, whereas every actual frequency has last coordinate $-\omega_j<0$, so no such partner is among the actual frequencies. If the three actual frequencies were not all equal, some frequency group among three nonzero terms would be a singleton; its vector coefficient would be $\pm A_j\ne0$, contradicting the lemma. Therefore all three actual waves match. If the reflected amplitude vanishes, the remaining two nonzero coefficients likewise require $\lambda_i=\lambda_t$; no conclusion about the zero wave's arbitrary labels follows. This proves (a) and the absent-wave qualification. For (b), each matched wavevector is $\kappa+(k_j\cdot n)n$, so it lies in the declared complex span; in the real case this is ordinary real coplanarity. For (c), the real dispersion relations give $|k_i|=|k_r|=\omega/v_1$ and $|k_t|=\omega/v_2$. The common tangential magnitude is $|k_j|\sin\theta_j$, hence $\theta_r=\theta_i$ by injectivity of sine on $[0,\pi/2]$, and $(\omega/v_1)\sin\theta_i=(\omega/v_2)\sin\theta_t$, i.e. the product form of Snell's law. Division by $\sin\theta_i$ is made only for positive incidence angle; normal incidence is covered by the product identity. The outgoing/non-growth normal root is a declared selection, not used in the frequency-independence proof. The interface conditions remain explicit assumptions on the noncompact plane, with no use of the compact jump theorem's distributional clause and no inherited choice principle. ∎

before.title: Conducting-medium propagation: the exact attenuation constant, the skin depth and its good- and poor-conductor regimes
before.statement: Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] in the isotropic scalar case at rest in the laboratory frame with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma>0$, the fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and the plane-wave structure of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: let $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, $n$ a unit vector and $k=\lambda n$, $\lambda\in\mathbb C$, and let $E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}\bigr)$ be a plane-wave field satisfying the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b) with $k\cdot e=0$. Put $a:=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}>0$, $b:=\mu\sigma\omega>0$, $r:=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and let $p,q>0$ be the quantities of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Then: (a) [Exact propagation constant and decay] $\lambda^{2}=k\cdot k=\varepsilon\mu\omega^{2}+i\mu\sigma\omega=a+ib$, so $\lambda=\pm(p+iq)$; if $x_3':=n\cdot x$, then for $\lambda=p+iq$ $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}\,\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(p x_3'-\omega t)}\bigr),$$ so the field oscillates with wavenumber $p$ and its amplitude decays in the direction of increasing $x_3'$ at the exact rate $q$; with $\lambda=-(p+iq)$ the same formula holds with $e^{q x_3'}$, which grows in that direction, so the decaying branch is the one with $\lambda=p+iq$, in agreement with the selection rule of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](b). (b) [Exact skin depth] $q^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}-a\bigr)/2$, $p^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)/2$, $pq=b/2=\mu\sigma\omega/2$, and the skin depth of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]] equals the exact closed expression $$\delta(\omega)=\frac{1}{q}=\frac{\sqrt{2\,(r+a)}}{b}=\frac{\sqrt{2\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)}}{\mu\sigma\omega}.$$ (c) [Good-conductor regime] put $t:=a/b=\varepsilon\omega/\sigma>0$. For every $t\le1/4$ the exact value satisfies the explicit bounds $$\bigl|q-\sqrt{b/2}\bigr|\le2t\sqrt{b/2}=\frac{2\varepsilon\omega}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\mu\sigma\omega}{2}},\qquad \bigl|\delta-\sqrt{2/b}\bigr|\le4t\sqrt{2/b}=\frac{4\varepsilon\omega}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\mu\sigma\omega}} ;$$ equivalently $\delta=\sqrt{2/(\mu\sigma\omega)}\,\bigl(1+O(\varepsilon\omega/\sigma)\bigr)$ in the declared regime $\varepsilon\omega/\sigma\le1/4$, with the displayed explicit remainder bounds. (d) [Poor-conductor regime] put $t':=b/a=\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega)>0$. For every $t'\le1/2$ the exact value satisfies $$\Bigl|q-\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{4}\cdot\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}},\qquad\Bigl|\delta-\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}},$$ so in this regime $\delta$ is frequency-independent up to the displayed relative error $O\bigl((\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega))^{2}\bigr)$. (e) [Phase relation for a real amplitude] if $e\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\lambda=p+iq$, then $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}e\cos(px_3'-\omega t),\qquad H(x,t)=\frac{e^{-q x_3'}}{\mu\omega}\bigl(p\cos(px_3'-\omega t)-q\sin(px_3'-\omega t)\bigr)\,(n\times e),$$ and the ratio of the quadrature to the in-phase coefficient is $q/p=\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t$ with $1-2t\le q/p\le1$ for every $t\le1/2$; in particular $q/p\to1$ as $t\downarrow0$, so in the good-conductor regime the magnetic field is asymptotically in quadrature with the electric field. (f) [Limits and scope] for $\sigma=0$ one has $b=0$, $q=0$, no attenuation and $\delta=+\infty$, and the approximations of (c) and (d) are not applicable; the ideal-conductor limit $\sigma\to\infty$ is not covered by this theorem, which works inside the finite-Ohmic branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] (a separate boundary model is needed for an ideal conductor); the frequency dependence of $\sigma$ (Drude or other) is not supplied, and $\sigma$ is the declared constant of the branch; the conclusions are exact identities for the ideal plane-wave field and carry no empirical content, no measured conductivity and no claim about any laboratory field.
before.strategy: (a): clause (c) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] gives $k\cdot k=\varepsilon\mu\omega^{2}+i\mu\sigma\omega$; with $k=\lambda n$ and $n$ a unit vector this is $\lambda^{2}=a+ib$, whose two roots are $\pm(p+iq)$ by the explicit square-root formula of [[thm-every-complex-number-has-a-square-root]] used in [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](b) (the verification $p^{2}-q^{2}=a$, $2pq=b$ is that of the definition). Writing $k\cdot x=\lambda\,x_3'$ and $e^{i\lambda x_3'}=e^{ipx_3'}e^{-qx_3'}$ real-extracts to the displayed factorization ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); for $\lambda=-(p+iq)$ the exponent $e^{qx_3'}$ grows in the $+n$ direction. (c): write $q^{2}=\frac{b}{2}\bigl(\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t\bigr)$ with $t=a/b$ and $\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t=\bigl(\sqrt{1+t^{2}}+t\bigr)^{-1}$; since $1\le\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\le1+t$ for $t\ge0$ one gets $\frac{1}{1+2t}\le\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t\le\frac{1}{1+t}\le1$, and $\frac{1}{1+2t}\ge1-2t$ ([[prop-of-multiply-inequalities]], [[lem-of-sign-rules]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]]). (d): with $s:=b/a$ one has $q^{2}=\frac{a}{2}(\sqrt{1+s^{2}}-1)$ and $q/q_{t}=\sqrt{2/(1+\sqrt{1+s^{2}})}$ for $q_{t}=\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\mu/\varepsilon}=\sqrt a\,s/2$, so $q\le q_{t}$ and, since $\sqrt{1+s^{2}}\le1+s^{2}/2$, $q/q_{t}\ge1/\sqrt{1+s^{2}/4}\ge1-s^{2}/4$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]], [[prop-of-multiply-inequalities]]); hence $|q-q_{t}|\le(s^{2}/4)q_{t}$. For $\delta=1/q$ and $\delta_{t}=1/q_{t}$ one has $\delta/\delta_{t}\le1/(1-s^{2}/4)\le1+s^{2}/2$ whenever $s^{2}/4\le1/2$, which holds for $s\le1/2$; this gives the second displayed bound. The identification $\sqrt a=\omega\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}$ and $s/2=\sigma/(2\varepsilon\omega)$ produce the stated coefficients. (e): with $e$ real, $h=\lambda(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)=(p+iq)(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)$ from clause (c) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]], and real extraction gives $H=e^{-qx_3'}\bigl(p\cos(px_3'-\omega t)-q\sin(px_3'-\omega t)\bigr)(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)$ and $E=e^{-qx_3'}e\cos(px_3'-\omega t)$; the ratio is $q/p=\sqrt{(r-a)/(r+a)}=\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t$ (rationalize and use $t=a/b$), and $1-2t\le\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t\le1$ was established in (c). (f) is a scope statement: at $b=0$ the formulas of (b)-(e) reduce to $q=0$, $\delta=+\infty$ by the convention of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](c), and the regimes of (c), (d) are void. No choice principle is used. ∎

after.title: Conducting-medium propagation: the exact attenuation constant, the skin depth and its good- and poor-conductor regimes
after.statement: Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] in the isotropic scalar case at rest in the laboratory frame with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma>0$, the fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and the plane-wave structure of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: let $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, $n$ a unit vector and $k=\lambda n$, $\lambda\in\mathbb C$, and let $E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}\bigr)$ be a plane-wave field satisfying the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b) with $k\cdot e=0$. Put $a:=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}>0$, $b:=\mu\sigma\omega>0$, $r:=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and let $p,q>0$ be the quantities of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Then: (a) [Exact propagation constant and decay] $\lambda^{2}=k\cdot k=\varepsilon\mu\omega^{2}+i\mu\sigma\omega=a+ib$, so $\lambda=\pm(p+iq)$; if $x_3':=n\cdot x$, then for $\lambda=p+iq$ $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}\,\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(p x_3'-\omega t)}\bigr),$$ so the field oscillates with wavenumber $p$ and its amplitude decays in the direction of increasing $x_3'$ at the exact rate $q$; with $\lambda=-(p+iq)$ the exact formula is $E(x,t)=e^{q x_3'}\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(-p x_3'-\omega t)})$, which grows in that direction, so the decaying branch is the one with $\lambda=p+iq$, in agreement with the selection rule of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](b). (b) [Exact skin depth] $q^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}-a\bigr)/2$, $p^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)/2$, $pq=b/2=\mu\sigma\omega/2$, and the skin depth of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]] equals the exact closed expression $$\delta(\omega)=\frac{1}{q}=\frac{\sqrt{2\,(r+a)}}{b}=\frac{\sqrt{2\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)}}{\mu\sigma\omega}.$$ (c) [Good-conductor regime] put $t:=a/b=\varepsilon\omega/\sigma>0$. For every $t\le1/4$ the exact value satisfies the explicit bounds $$\bigl|q-\sqrt{b/2}\bigr|\le2t\sqrt{b/2}=\frac{2\varepsilon\omega}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\mu\sigma\omega}{2}},\qquad \bigl|\delta-\sqrt{2/b}\bigr|\le4t\sqrt{2/b}=\frac{4\varepsilon\omega}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\mu\sigma\omega}} ;$$ equivalently $\delta=\sqrt{2/(\mu\sigma\omega)}\,\bigl(1+O(\varepsilon\omega/\sigma)\bigr)$ in the declared regime $\varepsilon\omega/\sigma\le1/4$, with the displayed explicit remainder bounds. (d) [Poor-conductor regime] put $t':=b/a=\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega)>0$. For every $t'\le1/2$ the exact value satisfies $$\Bigl|q-\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{4}\cdot\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}},\qquad\Bigl|\delta-\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}},$$ so in this regime $\delta$ is frequency-independent up to the displayed relative error $O\bigl((\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega))^{2}\bigr)$. (e) [Phase relation for a real amplitude] if $e\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\lambda=p+iq$, then $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}e\cos(px_3'-\omega t),\qquad H(x,t)=\frac{e^{-q x_3'}}{\mu\omega}\bigl(p\cos(px_3'-\omega t)-q\sin(px_3'-\omega t)\bigr)\,(n\times e),$$ and the ratio of the quadrature to the in-phase coefficient is $q/p=\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t$ with $1-2t\le q/p\le1$ for every $t\le1/2$; in particular $q/p\to1$ as $t\downarrow0$, so the magnetic scalar factor is $\sqrt{p^2+q^2}\cos(px_3'-\omega t+\eta)$ with $\eta:=\arctan(q/p)\to\pi/4$ (45 degrees), not a 90-degree quadrature phase shift. At fixed position with the $e^{-i\omega t}$ convention this corresponds to the stated signed $+\eta$ phase in the decreasing phase variable. (f) [Limits and scope] for $\sigma=0$ one has $b=0$, $q=0$, no attenuation and $\delta=+\infty$, and the approximations of (c) and (d) are not applicable; the ideal-conductor limit $\sigma\to\infty$ is not covered by this theorem, which works inside the finite-Ohmic branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] (a separate boundary model is needed for an ideal conductor); the frequency dependence of $\sigma$ (Drude or other) is not supplied, and $\sigma$ is the declared constant of the branch; the conclusions are exact identities for the ideal plane-wave field and carry no empirical content, no measured conductivity and no claim about any laboratory field.

For $\delta=1/q$ and $\delta_{t}=1/q_{t}$ one has $\delta/\delta_{t}\le1/(1-s^{2}/4)\le1+s^{2}/2$ whenever $s^{2}/4\le1/2$, which holds for $s\le1/2$; this gives the second displayed bound. (e): with $e$ real, $h=\lambda(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)=(p+iq)(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)$ from clause (c) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]], and real extraction gives $H=e^{-qx_3'}\bigl(p\cos(px_3'-\omega t)-q\sin(px_3'-\omega t)\bigr)(n\times e)/(\mu\omega)$ and $E=e^{-qx_3'}e\cos(px_3'-\omega t)$; the ratio is $q/p=\sqrt{(r-a)/(r+a)}=\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t$ (rationalize and use $t=a/b$), and $1-2t\le\sqrt{1+t^{2}}-t\le1$ was established in (c). Put $\eta=\arctan(q/p)$ using [[def-principal-inverse-tangent]]. Since $p,q>0$, $\cos\eta=p/\sqrt{p^2+q^2}$ and $\sin\eta=q/\sqrt{p^2+q^2}$; [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives $p\cos\theta-q\sin\theta=\sqrt{p^2+q^2}\cos(\theta+\eta)$. before.title: Normal-incidence amplitudes and the flux budget, with the Ohmic transmitting medium
before.statement: Assume the setting of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] at normal incidence: medium 1 in $\{x_3<0\}$ with $\varepsilon_1,\mu_1>0$, $\sigma_1=0$, medium 2 in $\{x_3>0\}$ with $\varepsilon_2,\mu_2>0$ and either $\sigma_2=0$ (lossless) or $\sigma_2>0$ (Ohmic), both homogeneous and at rest in the laboratory chart, with the plane interface $S=\{x_3=0\}$ and normal $n=e_3$. Let $\omega_i,\omega_r,\omega_t>0$ and let three plane waves of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] be given with wavevectors $k_i=k_1n$ ($k_1>0$), $k_r=-k_1n$ and $k_t=k\,n$, where for $\sigma_2=0$ one takes $k=\omega_t/v_2>0$ and for $\sigma_2>0$ one takes $k=\kappa_2(\omega_t)=p+iq$ with the complex propagation constant of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]; amplitudes $e_i,e_r,e_t\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ and $h_j=k_j\times e_j/(\mu_j\omega_j)$ satisfying the conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)-(c) in their media, and the four stationary interface identities of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] holding on $\mathbb R^{2}\times I$ for a nonempty open interval $I$. Then: (a) [Common frequency] $\omega_i=\omega_r=\omega_t=:\omega$ for some $\omega>0$ ([[pthm-em-phase-matching]](a)). (b) [Amplitude system and solution] all three electric amplitudes are tangential to $S$, and the two tangential interface identities reduce to $$e_i+e_r=e_t,\qquad Y_1\,(e_i-e_r)=Y_2\,e_t,\qquad Y_1:=\frac{k_1}{\mu_1\omega}>0,\qquad Y_2:=\frac{k}{\mu_2\omega};$$ hence $e_r=r\,e_i$ and $e_t=t\,e_i$ with the complex scalars $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ in particular the reflected and transmitted electric phasors are parallel to the incident one (normal-incidence polarisation preservation), and $r,t\ne0$. (c) [Lossless transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2=0$ then $Y_2=1/Z_2>0$ with $Z_2=\sqrt{\mu_2/\varepsilon_2}$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]], so $$r=\frac{Z_2-Z_1}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,\qquad t=\frac{2Z_2}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,$$ in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]; the period-$T$ averaged normal fluxes of the stored-energy model, $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](d), [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]), are $\langle S_i\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_i|^{2}}{2Z_1}$, $\langle S_r\cdot n\rangle=-\frac{|e_r|^{2}}{2Z_1}$ and $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_t|^{2}}{2Z_2}$, and with $R:=r^{2}$, $T:=\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}t^{2}=\frac{4Z_1Z_2}{(Z_1+Z_2)^{2}}$ one has $R+T=1$; $R$ is the reflected and $T$ the transmitted fraction of the incident normal averaged flux. (d) [Ohmic transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2>0$ then $Y_2=\kappa_2(\omega)/(\mu_2\omega)$ has $\operatorname{Re}Y_2=q/(\mu_2\omega)>0$, and $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad |r|^{2}+\frac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^{2}=1 .$$ The second summand is the fraction of the incident period-averaged normal flux that enters the conductor at the interface; the transmitted field has the exact decay factor $e^{-qx_3}$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](c) applied to $k=p+iq$) and, by the Ohmic dissipation clause of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]], the entering flux is absorbed in the conductor: the reflected fraction $|r|^{2}$ and the absorbed fraction $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^{2}$ add to $1$. (e) [Scope] no existence or uniqueness of interface-consistent data, no oblique incidence, no anisotropic or dispersive media, no ideal conductor ($\sigma_2=\infty$), no nonlinear response and no empirical claim is made. The interface identities are the stationary plane-interface conditions of the model, supplied for compact interfaces by [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]; the flux identities are the model's stored-energy and Ohmic-dissipation reading, not an observational claim.
before.strategy:
(a): the waves satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] (nonzero amplitudes, $k_i\cdot n=k_1>0$, $k_r\cdot n=-k_1<0$, $k_t\cdot n=k

after.title: Normal-incidence amplitudes and the flux budget, with the Ohmic transmitting medium
after.statement: Assume the following plane-interface material setting, with the same explicitly adopted stationary interface identities as [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] (including its absent-wave qualification), at normal incidence: medium 1 in $\{x_3<0\}$ with $\varepsilon_1,\mu_1>0$, $\sigma_1=0$, medium 2 in $\{x_3>0\}$ with $\varepsilon_2,\mu_2>0$ and either $\sigma_2=0$ (lossless) or $\sigma_2>0$ (Ohmic), both homogeneous and at rest in the laboratory chart, with the plane interface $S=\{x_3=0\}$ and normal $n=e_3$. Let $\omega_i,\omega_r,\omega_t>0$ and let three plane waves of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] be given with wavevectors $k_i=k_1n$ ($k_1>0$), $k_r=-k_1n$ and $k_t=k\,n$, where for $\sigma_2=0$ one takes $k=\omega_t/v_2>0$ and for $\sigma_2>0$ one takes $k=\kappa_2(\omega_t)=p+iq$ with the complex propagation constant of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]; amplitudes $e_i\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ and $e_r,e_t\in\mathbb C^{3}$ and $h_j=k_j\times e_j/(\mu_j\omega_j)$ satisfying the conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)-(c) in their media, and the four stationary interface identities of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] holding on $\mathbb R^{2}\times I$ for a nonempty open interval $I$. Then: (a) [Common frequency] The transmitted amplitude is nonzero and $\omega_i=\omega_t=:\omega$ for some $\omega>0$. If $e_r\ne0$, then $\omega_r=\omega$ as well; if $e_r=0$, assign $\omega_r=\omega$ conventionally, since an absent field cannot determine a frequency. Matching is proved directly from the interface characters, so the lossless-only physical scope of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] is not used to infer the Ohmic branch. (b) [Amplitude system and solution] all three electric amplitudes are tangential to $S$, and the two tangential interface identities reduce to $$e_i+e_r=e_t,\qquad Y_1\,(e_i-e_r)=Y_2\,e_t,\qquad Y_1:=\frac{k_1}{\mu_1\omega}>0,\qquad Y_2:=\frac{k}{\mu_2\omega};$$ hence $e_r=r\,e_i$ and $e_t=t\,e_i$ with the complex scalars $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ in particular the reflected and transmitted electric phasors are parallel to the incident one (normal-incidence polarisation preservation), and $t\ne0$. The reflection coefficient is zero exactly when $Y_1=Y_2$, in particular at a lossless impedance-matched interface; the zero reflected field remains part of the theorem. (c) [Lossless transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2=0$ then $Y_2=1/Z_2>0$ with $Z_2=\sqrt{\mu_2/\varepsilon_2}$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]], so $$r=\frac{Z_2-Z_1}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,\qquad t=\frac{2Z_2}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,$$ in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]; the period-$T$ averaged normal fluxes of the stored-energy model, $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](d), [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]), are $\langle S_i\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_i|^{2}}{2Z_1}$, $\langle S_r\cdot n\rangle=-\frac{|e_r|^{2}}{2Z_1}$ and $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_t|^{2}}{2Z_2}$, and with $R:=r^{2}$, $T:=\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}t^{2}=\frac{4Z_1Z_2}{(Z_1+Z_2)^{2}}$ one has $R+T=1$; $R$ is the reflected and $T$ the transmitted fraction of the incident normal averaged flux. (d) [Ohmic transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2>0$ then $Y_2=\kappa_2(\omega)/(\mu_2\omega)$ has $\operatorname{Re}Y_2=p/(\mu_2\omega)>0$, and $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad |r|^{2}+\frac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^{2}=1 .$$ The second summand is the fraction of the incident period-averaged normal flux that enters the conductor at the interface; the transmitted field has the exact decay factor $e^{-qx_3}$ (the explicit factorization $e^{i(p+iq)x_3}=e^{-qx_3}e^{ipx_3}$) and, by the Ohmic dissipation clause of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]], the entering flux is absorbed in the conductor: the reflected fraction $|r|^{2}$ and the absorbed fraction $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^{2}$ add to $1$. (e) [Scope] no existence or uniqueness of interface-consistent data, no oblique incidence, no anisotropic or dispersive media, no ideal conductor ($\sigma_2=\infty$), no nonlinear response and no empirical claim is made. The interface identities are the stationary plane-interface conditions of the model, supplied for compact interfaces by [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]; the flux identities are the model's stored-energy and Ohmic-dissipation reading, not an observational claim.
after.strategy:
(a): transversality with the nonzero normal wave numbers makes every electric amplitude tangential. The nonzero incident coefficient cannot be cancelled alone. Apply [[lem-em-exponential-character-open-set-independence]](b) to the tangential electric and magnetic traces, whose actual frequencies are $-\omega_j<0$. If $e_t=0$, the electric trace requires a nonzero reflected wave at the incident frequency with $e_r=-e_i$, but the magnetic trace then gives $Y_1(e_i-e_r)=2Y_1e_i=0$, impossible. Thus $e_t
e0$. Any distinct grouping of two or three actual nonzero waves has a singleton nonzero electric coefficient and contradicts character independence; hence incident and transmitted frequencies match, and reflected frequency matches when reflected amplitude is nonzero. Assign the common frequency conventionally to an absent reflected wave. This argument works for both lossless and Ohmic medium2 because the interface spatial phase is zero and all frequencies are positive. (b): the amplitude equations of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] give $h_i=Y_1n	imes e_i$, $h_r=-Y_1n	imes e_r$, $h_t=Y_2n	imes e_t$. Injectivity of real-part encoding at positive frequency makes the tangential boundary identities precisely $e_i+e_r=e_t$ and $Y_1(e_i-e_r)=Y_2e_t$. Since $Y_1>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}Y_2>0$, $Y_1+Y_2
e0$; [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]] applied componentwise yields $r,t$. The numerator of $t$ is $2Y_1
e0$; the numerator of $r$ can vanish and does so exactly for $Y_2=Y_1$. In the Ohmic branch $q>0$, so $\operatorname{Im}Y_2>0$ and $r
e0$, whereas the matched lossless branch has $r=0$. (c): $Y_j=1/Z_j>0$ in the lossless branch gives the stated real formulas. [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](d) gives the three signed normal fluxes (with zero flux for a zero reflected amplitude), and [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]](b),(d) gives $R+T=1$. Only the local stored-energy/flux clauses of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] are consumed. (d): $k=p+iq$, $p,q>0$ and $2pq=\mu_2\sigma_2\omega$ give $\operatorname{Re}Y_2=p/(\mu_2\omega)>0$, and the same algebra lemma yields the complex flux budget. Direct period averaging using [[lem-em-period-average]] gives the transmitted normal flux per unit transverse area $F(z)=p|e_t|^2e^{-2qz}/(2\mu_2\omega)$ and the Ohmic dissipation density $d(z)=\sigma_2|e_t|^2e^{-2qz}/2$. The identity $2pq=\mu_2\sigma_2\omega$ gives $F'(z)=-d(z)$, consistent with [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]](b). For every $L>0$, the integrand $d$ is continuous on $[0,L]$ and Riemann integrable by [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]] in dimension1; the exponential antiderivative is differentiable through both endpoints. The fundamental theorem [[thm-ftc-second-part]] applied to the exponential antiderivative gives $\int_0^L d(z)\,dz=\sigma_2|e_t|^2(1-e^{-2qL})/(4q)=F(0)-F(L)$. Since $q>0$, $e^{-2qL}	o0$; defining the improper integral by this limit as in [[def-improper-integral-at-infinity]], $\int_0^\infty d(z)\,dz=\sigma_2|e_t|^2/(4q)=F(0)$. This is absorbed flux per unit transverse area, never total energy or power over the infinite plane. The exact convergent exponential integral establishes the absorption statement without integrating an unbounded three-dimensional volume. The boundary and material laws remain adopted model premises; no fixed-volume or weak-source clause is used and no choice principle is inherited. ∎

before.statement:
Assume the setting of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]]: two homogeneous isotropic lossless scalar media at rest (medium 1 in $\{x_3<0\}$, constants $\varepsilon_1,\mu_1>0$; medium 2 in $\{x_3>0\}$, constants $\varepsilon_2,\mu_2>0$; both $\sigma=0$), the plane interface $S=\{x_3=0\}$ with normal $n=e_3$, and the plane-wave structure of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]. before.strategy: Polarisation data: for (s), $e_j=E_j\hat y$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=E_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)=0$ (because $k_j=\kappa+k_{j3}n$ and $\hat y\perp\kappa,n$); for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=0$ as well, and $k_j\times e_j=k_j\times\bigl(-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)\bigr)=H_j\bigl[(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y-k_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)\bigr]/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=H_j(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=\omega\mu_jh_j$ using $k_j\cdot k_j=\varepsilon_j\mu_j\omega^{2}$ and $k_j\cdot\hat y=0$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)). So both polarisations satisfy the amplitude conditions in the respective media. (a): with the common interface phase the tangential electric identity is the coefficient identity $e^{\tau}_i+e^{\tau}_r=e^{\tau}_t$ (where $v^{\tau}=v-(v\cdot n)n$); for (s) this is $E_i\hat y+E_r\hat y=E_t\hat y$, i.e. the scalar identity; for (p) the tangential part of $e_j$ is $(e_j\cdot\hat x)\hat x$ because $e_j$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$ (as $k_j\times\hat y\perp\hat y$ and $k_j\in\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$), so the identity is $E^{(p)}_i+E^{(p)}_r=E^{(p)}_t$. The tangential magnetic identity $n\times h_i+n\times h_r=n\times h_t$ similarly becomes, after taking components in the fixed direction and expressing $h_j$ through the electric amplitude: for (s), $h_j=(k_j\times e_j)/(\mu_j\omega)$ has tangential component in the $\hat\kappa$-direction equal to $-k_{j3}E_j/(\mu_j\omega)$ (the reflected sign included, since $k_{r3}=-k_{13}$), which yields $Y^{s}_1(E^{s}_i-E^{s}_r)=Y^{s}_2E^{s}_t$ with $Y^{s}_j=k_{j3}/(\mu_j\omega)$; for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ has $\hat\kappa$-component $k_{j3}H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and the magnetic identity $H_i+H_r=H_t$ gives, after expressing $H_j$ in the amplitudes, $Y^{p}_1(E^{p}_i-E^{p}_r)=Y^{p}_2E^{p}_t$ with $Y^{p}_j=\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3}$; both are instances of the two-equation system of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]], whose clause (a) gives the displayed $r_\chi,t_\chi$ (the determinant $Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2$ is nonzero in each branch: in the propagating branch both are real positive, in the evanescent branch the real part of the sum is $Y^{\chi}_1>0$). (b): the real-propagation statement is [[pthm-em-phase-matching]](c) applied with the common $(\kappa,\omega)$; $Y^{s}_j=k_{j3}/(\mu_j\omega)>0$ and $Y^{p}_j=\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3}>0$ are real because $k_{i3}=k_{r3}=k_{13}>0$ and $k_{t3}>0$. The flux identities are clauses (d),(e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: for (s) the normal flux of wave $j$ is $|e_j|^{2}k_{j3}/(2\mu_j\omega)=Y^{s}_j|E^{s}_j|^{2}/2$; for (p), $|e_j|=|k_j||H_j|/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and $|k_j|^{2}k_{j3}/(2\mu_j\omega\varepsilon_j^{2})=|E^{p}_j|^{2}Y^{p}_j/2$. Substituting the amplitudes gives $R_\chi+T_\chi=1$ by [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]](b) with real positive $Y^{\chi}_j$. (c): $r_\chi=0$ is equivalent to $Y^{\chi}_1=Y^{\chi}_2$ by clause (a); for $\mu_1=\mu_2$ and real positive admittances, $Y^{s}_1=Y^{s}_2$ and Snell's law imply $|k_i|=|k_t|$ and hence $n_1=n_2$, so for $n_1\ne n_2$ the $s$-amplitude does not vanish; for (p) with $\mu_1=\mu_2$ one has $Y^{p}_j=\sqrt{\varepsilon_j/\mu}/\cos\theta_j$ and $Y^{p}_1=Y^{p}_2$ together with $n_1\sin\theta_i=n_2\sin\theta_t$ is equivalent to $n_1\cos\theta_t=n_2\cos\theta_i$ and to $\theta_i+\theta_t=\pi/2$, i.e. to $\tan\theta_i=n_2/n_1$ with $\theta_i\in(0,\pi/2)$; uniqueness follows because $\theta\mapsto\tan\theta$ is strictly increasing on $(0,\pi/2)$, and the angle is admissible because $\sin\theta_t=n_1/\sqrt{n_1^{2}+n_2^{2}}<1$. (d): for $|\kappa|>K_2$ the selection $k_{t3}=i\beta$ gives $Y^{s}_2=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)=i\beta/(\mu_2\omega)$ and $Y^{p}_2=\varepsilon_2\omega/(i\beta)=-i\varepsilon_2\omega/\beta$, both purely imaginary ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]); clause (c) of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]] gives $|r_\chi|=1$ and $|t_\chi|^{2}=4(Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}/((Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}+|Y^{\chi}_2|^{2})>0$; the transmitted field structure, decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] applied to the transverse polarisations (the (s) case is the $e$ polarisation $n'\times\hat\kappa_0$ with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$; the (p) case is the corresponding $h$ polarisation). The reflected flux equals the incident flux because $|r_\chi|=1$. (e): $k_{t3}=0$ gives, in the (s) case, $Y^{s}_2=0$, hence $r_s=1$ and $|r_s|=1$; in the (p) case the transmitted tangential electric amplitude is $E^{p}_t=k_{t3}H_t/(\omega\varepsilon_2)=0$, so the first interface equation gives $E^{p}_r=-E^{p}_i$ and $|r_p|=1$; the normal transmitted flux vanishes because $k_{t3}=0$ enters it linearly. (f) is a scope statement. All divisions are by nonzero complex numbers; no choice principle is used. ∎
before.physical_scope: Conditional oblique-incidence Fresnel theorem for two homogeneous isotropic lossless scalar media at rest at a plane interface, under the stated interface identities: the TE and TM admittance systems, amplitude formulas, the flux budget $R_\chi+T_\chi=1$ in the propagating branch, the Brewster condition and the total-internal-reflection identities $|r_\chi|=1$ with decaying transmitted field. Excluded: absorbing, dispersive, anisotropic, moving or nonlinear media, the ideal conductor, existence or uniqueness of interface-consistent data, signal- and group-velocity claims, and all empirical claims.

after.title: Oblique-incidence TE and TM Fresnel amplitudes, the flux budget, Brewster's angle and total internal reflection

Here $Y_1^\chi>0$ uses the positive incident normal magnitude $k_{13}$, whereas the signed reflected component is $k_r\cdot n=-k_{13}$; $Y_1^\chi$ is not defined from that negative component. No $Y_2^p$ is defined at $k_{t3}=0$. hence, whenever $Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2
e0$, $$r_\chi:= rac{E^{\chi}_r}{E^{\chi}_i}= rac{Y^{\chi}_1-Y^{\chi}_2}{Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2},\qquad t_\chi:= rac{E^{\chi}_t}{E^{\chi}_i}= rac{2Y^{\chi}_1}{Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2}$$ ([[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]](a)); the reflected and transmitted amplitude symbols are defined by these fixed-direction conventions, and sign conventions for full vector amplitudes may reverse a reflected amplitude relative to this convention. (b) [Propagating branch and Snell's law] if $|\kappa|<K_2$ then all three wavevectors are real, $Y^{s}_j,Y^{p}_j>0$ are real, and with $	heta_j\in(0,\pi/2)$ defined by $\sin	heta_j=|\kappa|/|k_j|$ one has $	heta_r=	heta_i$ and $n_1\sin	heta_i=n_2\sin	heta_t$, $n_j=c(\varepsilon_j\mu_j)^{1/2}$ ([[pthm-em-phase-matching]](c), [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]); the period-averaged normal fluxes are $Y^{\chi}_1|E^{\chi}_i|^{2}/2$, $-Y^{\chi}_1|E^{\chi}_r|^{2}/2$ and $Y^{\chi}_2|E^{\chi}_t|^{2}/2$, so $$R_\chi:=|r_\chi|^{2},\qquad T_\chi:= rac{Y^{\chi}_2}{Y^{\chi}_1}|t_\chi|^{2},\qquad R_\chi+T_\chi=1 .$$ (c) [Brewster condition] In the finite-admittance branches, $r_\chi=0$ if and only if $Y^{\chi}_1=Y^{\chi}_2$; in particular, if $\mu_1=\mu_2$ and $|\kappa|<K_2$, for unequal indices $n_1

e0$ at that angle. For equal indices $n_1=n_2$ (and equal permeabilities), the media are identical, $Y_1^\chi=Y_2^\chi$ and $r_s=r_p=0$, $t_s=t_p=1$ for every allowed incidence angle; there is no unique distinguished Brewster angle. (d) [Total internal reflection] if $|\kappa|>K_2$ (which requires $n_1>n_2$, $|\kappa|=K_1\sin	heta_i$ with $	heta_i>	heta_c:=\arcsin(n_2/n_1)$ in the notation of (b)), then $Y^{s}_2=i eta/(\mu_2\omega)$ and $Y^{p}_2=-i\varepsilon_2\omega/ eta$ are purely imaginary, $$|r_s|=|r_p|=1,\qquad t_s,t_p
e0,\qquad |t_\chi|^{2}= rac{4(Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}}{(Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}+|Y^{\chi}_2|^{2}}>0,$$ the transmitted field decays as $e^{- eta x_3}$ and its period-averaged normal flux vanishes identically while its tangential averaged flux does not vanish ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](e)); the reflected wave carries the whole incident normal averaged flux. (e) [Critical angle] if $|\kappa|=K_2$ then $k_{t3}=0$: the transmitted wave travels along the interface, its tangential electric amplitude vanishes in the (p) case and $Y^{s}_2=0$ in the (s) case, and $r_s=1$, $t_s=2$, $r_p=-1$, $t_p=0$ with vanishing transmitted normal averaged flux. The critical TM branch is solved from the nonsingular equations $E_i^p+E_r^p=k_{t3}H_t/(\omega\varepsilon_2)=0$ and $H_i+H_r=H_t$, not by dividing by $k_{t3}$; they give $H_r=H_i$ and $H_t=2H_i$. Excluded: anisotropic media, complex $\varepsilon$ or $\mu$ and absorption in either medium (only the lossless dielectric case with the evanescent transmitted branch is covered), dispersive media, moving media, the ideal conductor, nonlinear response, and all claims about signal speeds, group velocities, information transfer or empirical data. The statements for $Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2=0$ (which cannot occur in the stated branches, where $\operatorname{Re}Y^{\chi}_1>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}Y^{\chi}_2\ge0$) are excluded; the notation 'angle of refraction' is used only where $k_t$ is real.
after.strategy: Polarisation data: for (s), $e_j=E_j\hat y$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=E_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)=0$ (because $k_j=\kappa+k_{j3}n$ and $\hat y\perp\kappa,n$); for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=0$ as well, and $k_j\times e_j=k_j\times\bigl(-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)\bigr)=H_j\bigl[(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y-k_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)\bigr]/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=H_j(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=\omega\mu_jh_j$ using $k_j\cdot k_j=\varepsilon_j\mu_j\omega^{2}$ and $k_j\cdot\hat y=0$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)). So both polarisations satisfy the amplitude conditions in the respective media. (a): with the common interface phase the tangential electric identity is the coefficient identity $e^{\tau}_i+e^{\tau}_r=e^{\tau}_t$ (where $v^{\tau}=v-(v\cdot n)n$); for (s) this is $E_i\hat y+E_r\hat y=E_t\hat y$, i.e. the scalar identity; for (p) the tangential part of $e_j$ is $(e_j\cdot\hat x)\hat x$ because $e_j$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$ (as $k_j\times\hat y\perp\hat y$ and $k_j\in\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$), so the identity is $E^{(p)}_i+E^{(p)}_r=E^{(p)}_t$. The tangential magnetic identity $n\times h_i+n\times h_r=n\times h_t$ similarly becomes, after taking components in the fixed direction and expressing $h_j$ through the electric amplitude: for (s), $h_j=(k_j\times e_j)/(\mu_j\omega)$ has tangential component in the $\hat\kappa$-direction equal to $-k_{j3}E_j/(\mu_j\omega)$ (the reflected sign included, since $k_{r3}=-k_{13}$), which yields $Y^{s}_1(E^{s}_i-E^{s}_r)=Y^{s}_2E^{s}_t$ with $Y^s_1=k_{13}/(\mu_1\omega)$, $Y^s_2=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)$; for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ has $\hat\kappa$-component $k_{j3}H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and the magnetic identity $H_i+H_r=H_t$ gives, after expressing $H_j$ in the amplitudes, $Y^{p}_1(E^{p}_i-E^{p}_r)=Y^{p}_2E^{p}_t$ with $Y^p_1=\varepsilon_1\omega/k_{13}$, $Y^p_2=\varepsilon_2\omega/k_{t3}$ for $k_{t3}\ne0$; both are instances of the two-equation system of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]], whose clause (a) gives the displayed $r_\chi,t_\chi$ (the determinant $Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2$ is nonzero in each branch: in the propagating branch both are real positive, in the evanescent branch the real part of the sum is $Y^{\chi}_1>0$). (b): the real-propagation statement is [[pthm-em-phase-matching]](c) applied with the common $(\kappa,\omega)$; $Y^{s}_j=k_{j3}/(\mu_j\omega)>0$ and $Y^{p}_j=\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3}>0$ are real because the admittance $Y_1$ uses the positive magnitude $k_{13}>0$, while the reflected signed component is $k_{r3}=-k_{13}$ and $k_{t3}>0$. The flux identities are clauses (d),(e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: for (s) the normal flux of wave $j$ is $|e_j|^{2}k_{j3}/(2\mu_j\omega)=Y^{s}_j|E^{s}_j|^{2}/2$; for (p), $E_j^p=k_{j3}H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and the normal flux is $k_{j3}|H_j|^2/(2\omega\varepsilon_j)=(\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3})|E_j^p|^2/2$. The latter coefficient is negative for the reflected wave; writing it as $-Y_1^p$ gives the signed reflected flux. Thus both polarisations use $+Y_1$ for incidence and $-Y_1$ for reflection, and $+Y_2$ for transmission. Substituting the amplitudes gives $R_\chi+T_\chi=1$ by [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]](b) with real positive $Y^{\chi}_j$. (c): Away from the critical TM branch, the finite-admittance formula gives $r_\chi=0$ exactly for $Y_1^\chi=Y_2^\chi$. For equal permeabilities and unequal positive indices, equality of TE admittances would imply $k_{13}=k_{t3}$ and hence $K_1=K_2$, impossible. The TM equality is $n_1\cos\theta_t=n_2\cos\theta_i$ together with Snell $n_1\sin\theta_i=n_2\sin\theta_t$. Squaring and eliminating $\sin\theta_t$ gives $(n_1^2-n_2^2)[n_2^2-(n_1^2+n_2^2)\sin^2\theta_i]=0$. For unequal indices divide only by the nonzero first factor to obtain $\sin^2\theta_i=n_2^2/(n_1^2+n_2^2)$ and $\tan\theta_i=n_2/n_1$; strict monotonicity of tangent on $(0,\pi/2)$ gives uniqueness, and $\sin\theta_t=n_1/\sqrt{n_1^2+n_2^2}<1$ proves admissibility. For equal indices and permeabilities the two media are identical: Snell gives $\theta_t=\theta_i$, both admittances agree at every allowed angle, and $r_s=r_p=0$, $t_s=t_p=1$. No uniqueness inference follows in that degenerate branch. (d): for $|\kappa|>K_2$ the selection $k_{t3}=i\beta$ gives $Y^{s}_2=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)=i\beta/(\mu_2\omega)$ and $Y^{p}_2=\varepsilon_2\omega/(i\beta)=-i\varepsilon_2\omega/\beta$, both purely imaginary ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]); clause (c) of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]] gives $|r_\chi|=1$ and $|t_\chi|^{2}=4(Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}/((Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}+|Y^{\chi}_2|^{2})>0$; the transmitted field structure, decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] applied to the transverse polarisations (the (s) case is the $e$ polarisation $n'\times\hat\kappa_0$ with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$; the (p) case is the corresponding $h$ polarisation). The reflected flux equals the incident flux because $|r_\chi|=1$. (e): At critical incidence solve without defining $Y_2^p$. The TE equations have $Y_2^s=0$, so $E_r^s=E_i^s$ and $E_t^s=2E_i^s$, giving $r_s=1$, $t_s=2$. For TM, $E_i^p=k_{13}H_i/(\omega\varepsilon_1)$, $E_r^p=-k_{13}H_r/(\omega\varepsilon_1)$ and $E_t^p=0$. The electric boundary identity forces $H_r=H_i$; the magnetic one gives $H_t=H_i+H_r=2H_i$. Thus $r_p=-1$, $t_p=0$ as ratios of the nonzero incident tangential electric amplitude. The transmitted electric vector is $-\kappa\times\hat y\,H_t/(\omega\varepsilon_2)$, a normal vector that need not vanish. Both transmitted normal fluxes are zero by direct $\operatorname{Re}(e_t\times\overline h_t)\cdot n/2$ calculation (or the real-wave normal factor $k_{t3}=0$). The four interface identities are consistent: the normal D jump for TM reduces to $H_t=H_i+H_r$, and the normal B jump for TE to $E_t^s=E_i^s+E_r^s$. All critical conclusions are therefore established by finite equations. (f) is a scope statement. All divisions are by nonzero complex numbers; no choice principle is used. ∎

before.statement: Adopt the isotropic scalar Ohmic branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] at rest and the exact quantities of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]] and [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]]. Let the declared parameters be $$\varepsilon=4\ \mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \mu=1\ \mathrm H\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \sigma=100\ \mathrm S\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \omega=3\ \mathrm s^{-1};$$ these are declared model parameters of the illustration, not measured values of any material. Then: (i) $a=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}=36$, $b=\mu\sigma\omega=300$, $r=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}=\sqrt{91296}$ and $t=a/b=3/25=0.12\le1/4$, so the good-conductor regime of [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]](c) applies; (ii) the exact propagation and attenuation constants are $p=\sqrt{(r+36)/2}$ and $q=\sqrt{(r-36)/2}$, with $pq=b/2=150$ exactly; the decimal evaluations $r\approx302.15228$, $p\approx13.00293$, $q\approx11.53586$ satisfy $q<\sqrt{b/2}=\sqrt{150}\approx12.24745$ with $$|q-\sqrt{150}|\approx0.71159\le 2t\sqrt{150}=0.24\sqrt{150}\approx2.93939,$$ and for the skin depth $\delta=1/q\approx0.08669$ against $\sqrt{2/b}=1/\sqrt{150}\approx0.08165$ one has $$|\delta-\sqrt{2/b}|\approx0.00504\le 4t\sqrt{2/b}=0.48\sqrt{2/b}\approx0.03919 .$$ Thus the exact skin depth satisfies the stated good-conductor bound with the margin predicted by the theorem. (iv) [Scope] the computation is an exact check of the stated inequalities for the declared dimensionless data; it reports no measurement, no material identification and no empirical claim, and the decimal evaluations are displayed only as approximate illustrations of the exact expressions.
before.strategy: Direct substitution in the theorem: $a=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}=1\cdot4\cdot9=36$ and $b=\mu\sigma\omega=1\cdot100\cdot3=300$; $r=\sqrt{36^{2}+300^{2}}=\sqrt{1296+90000}=\sqrt{91296}$; $t=36/300=3/25$; $pq=\sqrt{(r^{2}-a^{2})/4}=b/2=150$ by the exact identity of [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]](b). The two inequalities are the displayed bounds of that theorem specialised to $t=3/25$; the decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact radicals, computed as $r=\sqrt{91296}$, $q=\sqrt{(r-36)/2}$, $\delta=1/q$, and displayed to five decimals. The $\sigma=0$ clause is the convention $\delta=+\infty$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](c) together with $q=0$ at $b=0$. No empirical input or measurement enters.

before.title: The Brewster angle at an equal-permeability interface and the surviving $s$-reflection
before.statement: Adopt the setting of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with two lossless media at rest, equal permeabilities $\mu_1=\mu_2=:\mu>0$ and declared refractive indices $n_1=1$, $n_2=3/2$ (declared model parameters, not optical measurements), so that $\varepsilon_j=n_j^{2}/(c^{2}\mu)$ and $K_j=n_j\omega/c$ in the notation of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Then: (i) [Brewster angle] by [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](c) the TM amplitude vanishes exactly at the unique angle $\theta_B\in(0,\pi/2)$ with $\tan\theta_B=n_2/n_1=3/2$, i.e. $\sin\theta_B=3/\sqrt{13}$, $\cos\theta_B=2/\sqrt{13}$; the transmitted angle satisfies $n_1\sin\theta_B=n_2\sin\theta_t$, hence $\sin\theta_t=2/\sqrt{13}$, and $\theta_B+\theta_t=\pi/2$; (ii) [Amplitudes] at $\theta_i=\theta_B$ one has $Y^{p}_1=Y^{p}_2=\sqrt{13}/(2c\mu)$, hence $r_p=0$ and $t_p=1$; the remaining $s$-amplitudes are $Y^{s}_1=2/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$, $Y^{s}_2=9/(2\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ and $$r_s=\frac{2/\sqrt{13}-9/(2\sqrt{13})}{2/\sqrt{13}+9/(2\sqrt{13})}=-\frac{5}{13},\qquad t_s=\frac{8}{13};$$ (iii) [Flux budget] with $R_s=|r_s|^{2}=25/169$ and $T_s=(Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=(9/4)(64/169)=144/169$ one has $R_s+T_s=169/169=1$ exactly, while the TM channel has $R_p=0$, $T_p=1$; (iv) [Scope] the numbers are declared model parameters; the example is a deterministic computation of the classical interface model, reports no measurement, and the statement that the reflected beam is TM-polarised at the Brewster angle concerns exactly the TM channel of this idealisation (an unpolarised incident beam is not modelled here).
before.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]]: $K_j=n_j\omega/c$ and the admittances are $Y^{s}_j=k_{j3}/(\mu\omega)$, $Y^{p}_j=\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3}$ with $k_{13}=(\omega/c)\cos\theta_B=(2/\sqrt{13})(\omega/c)$ and, at $\theta_t$ with $\sin\theta_t=2/\sqrt{13}$, $k_{t3}=(3\omega/(2c))(3/\sqrt{13})=(9/(2\sqrt{13}))(\omega/c)$; hence $Y^{s}_1=2/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$, $Y^{s}_2=(9/4)Y^{s}_1=9/(2\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ and $Y^{p}_1=\varepsilon_1\omega/k_{13}=\sqrt{13}/(2c\mu)=Y^{p}_2$ (the equality $Y^{p}_1=Y^{p}_2$ is exactly the Brewster condition of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](c) and gives $r_p=(Y^{p}_1-Y^{p}_2)/(Y^{p}_1+Y^{p}_2)=0$, $t_p=1$). The $s$-amplitudes follow from the admittance formulas of that theorem by factoring $1/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ from numerator and denominator: $r_s=(4/2-9/2)/(4/2+9/2)=-5/13$ and $t_s=2\cdot(4/2)/(13/2)=8/13$; the flux identities are clause (b) of the same theorem: $T_s=(Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=(9/4)\cdot(64/169)=144/169$, and $25/169+144/169=1$ exactly. The angles: $\sin\theta_t=n_1\sin\theta_B/n_2=(2/3)(3/\sqrt{13})=2/\sqrt{13}=\cos\theta_B$ gives $\theta_B+\theta_t=\pi/2$. All numbers are exact rational or quadratic-irrational expressions; no empirical input, no measurement and no statistical claim is used.
before.physical_scope: Deterministic example of the oblique-incidence interface model for two declared lossless media with equal permeabilities and indices $n_1=1$, $n_2=3/2$: the unique Brewster angle $\tan\theta_B=n_2/n_1$, $r_p=0$, $t_p=1$, the surviving $s$-reflection $r_s=-5/13$ with $R_s+T_s=1$ exactly. Excluded: measured refractive indices, absorption, interfaces between unequal permeabilities, unpolarised-beam statistics and every empirical claim.

before.title: Total internal reflection: decaying transmitted field, vanishing normal flux and the reflection phase
before.statement: Adopt the setting of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with equal permeabilities $\mu_1=\mu_2=:\mu>0$ and declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ (declared model parameters, not measurements), and the transverse-electric polarisation $e_j=E_j\hat y$. Let the incidence angle be given by $\sin\theta_i=4/5$, which exceeds the critical angle $\theta_c$ with $\sin\theta_c=n_2/n_1=2/3$, so $|\kappa|=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)>(\omega/c)=K_2$. Then with $\beta=\sqrt{|\kappa|^{2}-K_2^{2}}=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$ and $k_{13}=(\omega/c)(3/2)(3/5)=(9/10)(\omega/c)$: (i) [Reflection] $Y^{s}_1=9/(10\mu c)$, $Y^{s}_2=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$ and $$r_s=\frac{9/10-i\sqrt{11}/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |r_s|=1,\qquad t_s=\frac{9/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |t_s|^{2}=\frac{324}{125};$$ the reflection factor is the phase $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$ with $\varphi=\arctan\!\bigl(2\sqrt{11}/9\bigr)\approx0.63525$ (about $36.40^\circ$), i.e. the reflected wave acquires the phase $-2\varphi\approx-1.2705$ (about $-72.79^\circ$); (ii) [Transmitted field] the transmitted field is $E_t(x,t)=e^{-\beta x_3}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(E_t\hat y\,e^{i(\kappa x_1-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with $\beta=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$: it decays by the factor $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}\approx0.51514$ when $x_3$ increases by $c/\omega$, its period-averaged normal flux vanishes identically, $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle\equiv0$, while its tangential averaged flux is positive, $\langle S_t\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle=e^{-2\beta x_3}\,\frac{(6/5)(\omega/c)|E_t|^{2}}{2\mu\omega}=e^{-2\beta x_3}\frac{3|E_t|^{2}}{5\mu c}$; (iii) [Flux budget] $|r_s|^{2}+(\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=1+0=1$, so the whole incident normal averaged flux is reflected, while the evanescent field carries a tangential averaged flux only; (iv) [Scope] the example is an exact deterministic computation of the lossless interface model for declared parameters; it reports no measurement, and the presence of a tangential evanescent flux is not a claim about information speed or signal propagation.
before.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](d): $K_1=(3/2)(\omega/c)$, $\kappa=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)$, $\beta=\sqrt{(36/25-1)}(\omega/c)=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$, $k_{13}=K_1\cos\theta_i=(3/2)(3/5)(\omega/c)$ (because $\cos\theta_i=3/5$), so $Y^{s}_1=k_{13}/(\mu\omega)=9/(10\mu c)$ and $Y^{s}_2=i\beta/(\mu\omega)=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$. Then $r_s=(Y^{s}_1-Y^{s}_2)/(Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2)$, whose numerator is the complex conjugate of its denominator, so $|r_s|=1$; $|t_s|^{2}=|2Y^{s}_1|^{2}/|Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2|^{2}=(81/25)/(81/100+11/25)=324/125$ by [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws|the modulus laws]]; the phase is the argument of the denominator and satisfies $\tan\varphi=(\sqrt{11}/5)/(9/10)=2\sqrt{11}/9$, hence $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$. The decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$ and the transverse-electric polarisation; the tangential-flux value is its displayed formula $|\kappa_0||e|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)=|\kappa||E_t|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)$ with $|\kappa|=(6/5)(\omega/c)$. The flux budget is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with $\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2=0$. The decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact expressions $\arctan(2\sqrt{11}/9)$ and $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}$. No empirical input is used.
before.physical_scope: Deterministic example of total internal reflection in the lossless interface model for declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ at $\sin\theta_i=4/5$: the unit-modulus reflection factor with its phase, the evanescent transmitted field with decay factor $e^{-\beta x_3}$, the vanishing normal and positive tangential averaged fluxes. Excluded: measured indices, absorption, information-speed or signal-propagation claims, and every empirical statement.

Then with $\beta=\sqrt{|\kappa|^{2}-K_2^{2}}=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$ and $k_{13}=(\omega/c)(3/2)(3/5)=(9/10)(\omega/c)$: (i) [Reflection] $Y^{s}_1=9/(10\mu c)$, $Y^{s}_2=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$ and $$r_s=\frac{9/10-i\sqrt{11}/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |r_s|=1,\qquad t_s=\frac{9/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |t_s|^{2}=\frac{324}{125};$$ the reflection factor is the phase $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$ with $\varphi=\arctan\!\bigl(2\sqrt{11}/9\bigr)\approx0.63514703$ (about $36.39124^\circ$), i.e. the reflected wave acquires the phase $-2\varphi\approx-1.27029406$ (about $-72.78249^\circ$); (ii) [Transmitted field] the transmitted field is $E_t(x,t)=e^{-\beta x_3}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(E_t\hat y\,e^{i(\kappa x_1-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with $\beta=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$: it decays by the factor $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}\approx0.51514$ when $x_3$ increases by $c/\omega$, its period-averaged normal flux vanishes identically, $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle\equiv0$, while its tangential averaged flux is positive, $\langle S_t\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle=e^{-2\beta x_3}\,\frac{(6/5)(\omega/c)|E_t|^{2}}{2\mu\omega}=e^{-2\beta x_3}\frac{3|E_t|^{2}}{5\mu c}$; (iii) [Flux budget] $|r_s|^{2}+(\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=1+0=1$, so the whole incident normal averaged flux is reflected, while the evanescent field carries a tangential averaged flux only; (iv) [Scope] the example is an exact deterministic computation of the lossless interface model for declared parameters; it reports no measurement, and the presence of a tangential evanescent flux is not a claim about information speed or signal propagation.
after.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](d): $K_1=(3/2)(\omega/c)$, $\kappa=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)$, $\beta=\sqrt{(36/25-1)}(\omega/c)=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$, $k_{13}=K_1\cos\theta_i=(3/2)(3/5)(\omega/c)$ (because $\cos\theta_i=3/5$), so $Y^{s}_1=k_{13}/(\mu\omega)=9/(10\mu c)$ and $Y^{s}_2=i\beta/(\mu\omega)=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$. Then $r_s=(Y^{s}_1-Y^{s}_2)/(Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2)$, whose numerator is the complex conjugate of its denominator, so $|r_s|=1$; $|t_s|^{2}=|2Y^{s}_1|^{2}/|Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2|^{2}=(81/25)/(81/100+11/25)=324/125$ by [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws|the modulus laws]]; the phase is the argument of the denominator and satisfies $\tan\varphi=(\sqrt{11}/5)/(9/10)=2\sqrt{11}/9$, hence $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$. The decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$ and the transverse-electric polarisation; the tangential-flux value is its displayed formula $|\kappa_0||e|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)=|\kappa||E_t|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)$ with $|\kappa|=(6/5)(\omega/c)$. The flux budget is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with $\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2=0$. The decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact expressions $\arctan(2\sqrt{11}/9)$ and $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}$. No empirical input is used.
after.physical_scope: Deterministic example of total internal reflection in the lossless interface model for declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ at $\sin\theta_i=4/5$: the unit-modulus reflection factor with its phase, the evanescent transmitted field with decay factor $e^{-\beta x_3}$, the vanishing normal and positive tangential averaged fluxes. Excluded: measured indices, absorption, information-speed or signal-propagation claims, and every empirical statement.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 author-hosted revision, 236 pp.)
references.locator: §7.4.2 printed pp. 191-193: total internal reflection beyond $\sin\theta_C=n_2/n_1$, the imaginary normal component of the transmitted wavevector and the decaying evanescent solution $E_{\mathrm{trans}}=E_T e^{(ik_T\cdot\hat z-\omega t)}e^{\mp\omega\alpha x/v_2}$; the explicit numbers here are evaluated from those formulas and the interface amplitudes, not copied from the source.

references.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall, 1999, 596-page retained scan)
references.locator: Problem 9.37 printed pp. 413-414: the evanescent transmitted field $E_T=E_{0T}e^{-Kz}e^{i(kx-\omega t)}$ with $k=(\omega/c)n_1\sin\theta_I$, $K=(\omega/c)\sqrt{n_1^{2}\sin^{2}\theta_I-n_2^{2}}$, the reflection coefficient of magnitude one for both polarisations and the statement that no energy is transmitted into medium 2 on average (part (f)); §9.3.3 printed pp. 388-390 for the amplitude formulas used. Retained scan with OCR noise; the displayed numbers were verified by the local computation in the batch notes.

## Statement

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Reals $x,y$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Apply the addition law to $x+iy$ and Euler's formula. [given]

1.2 Multiplicativity of modulus, the Pythagorean identity, and positivity of $e^x$ give the modulus formula. [given]

2.1 The defining quarter-turn value $\cos\pi=-1$ and $\sin\pi=0$ give Euler's identity. [given] ∎

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{n-1}):U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ in the componentwise Euclidean sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Then the **divergence** of $F$ is $\operatorname{div}F:=\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i$, the function $U\to\mathbb R$ whose value at $p$ is $\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i(p)$. The partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the sum is the finite sum used throughout [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Since each $\partial_iF_i$ is continuous on $U$, so is $\operatorname{div}F$.

Now let $n=3$ and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Following [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], write the three coordinates of a point and of a vector as $x,y,z$ rather than $0,1,2$, so that $F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ means $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2)$ and $\partial_x,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2$. With that naming, the **curl** of $F$ is $\operatorname{curl}F:=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, a map $U\to\mathbb R^3$ each of whose coordinates is continuous on $U$. In this naming the divergence reads $\operatorname{div}F=\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z$.

Both operators are defined pointwise from the first partial derivatives of the components, so no differentiability of $F$ beyond $C^1$ is used and no orientation or metric structure enters beyond the standard coordinates of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. For a $C^1$ scalar function $f$ on $U$, the gradient $\nabla f=(\partial_0f,\ldots,\partial_{n-1}f)$ is that of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; in the three-coordinate naming, $\nabla f=(\partial_xf,\partial_yf,\partial_zf)$.

## Definition

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{n-1}):U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ in the componentwise Euclidean sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Then the **divergence** of $F$ is $\operatorname{div}F:=\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i$, the function $U\to\mathbb R$ whose value at $p$ is $\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i(p)$. The partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the sum is the finite sum used throughout [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Since each $\partial_iF_i$ is continuous on $U$, so is $\operatorname{div}F$.

Now let $n=3$ and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Following [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], write the three coordinates of a point and of a vector as $x,y,z$ rather than $0,1,2$, so that $F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ means $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2)$ and $\partial_x,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2$. With that naming, the **curl** of $F$ is $\operatorname{curl}F:=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, a map $U\to\mathbb R^3$ each of whose coordinates is continuous on $U$. In this naming the divergence reads $\operatorname{div}F=\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z$.

Both operators are defined pointwise from the first partial derivatives of the components, so no differentiability of $F$ beyond $C^1$ is used and no orientation or metric structure enters beyond the standard coordinates of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. For a $C^1$ scalar function $f$ on $U$, the gradient $\nabla f=(\partial_0f,\ldots,\partial_{n-1}f)$ is that of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; in the three-coordinate naming, $\nabla f=(\partial_xf,\partial_yf,\partial_zf)$.

## Remarks

- **Why the curl is only defined in three coordinates.** If $A=JF-(JF)^{\mathsf T}$ with the row-component Jacobian convention, then the curl coordinates are $A_{zy}$, $A_{xz}$ and $A_{yx}$. Thus the curl is encoded, with fixed signs, by the three independent off-diagonal entries of $A$ (or by twice those entries if “antisymmetric part” means $A/2$). In $n$ coordinates there are $n(n-1)/2$ independent entries. Only at $n=3$ is that number again $n$, which is what allows the collection to be read as a vector in the same space. The divergence has no such restriction and is defined for every $n\ge1$.

- **The word "divergence" here is about vector fields.** It has nothing to do with the divergence of a sequence or of a series; the two senses share only the word.

- **Placement of the minus sign in the second coordinate.** Some presentations write the middle coordinate as $-(\partial_xF_z-\partial_zF_x)$. That is the same real number as $\partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z$, and the form displayed above is the one whose three coordinates read off the coordinate formula of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] in the same cyclic pattern.

object.title: Complex plane-wave fields: real parts of complex exponentials
object.statement: Fix $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, $\omega>0$ and $\mathbf e,\mathbf b\in\mathbb C^3$. Writing $\exp$ for the complex exponential, $\operatorname{Re}$ for the real part and $\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$ for the Euclidean inner product, define for each $t\in\mathbb R$ the real vector fields $$\mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf e\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr],\qquad \mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf b\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr]$$ on $\mathbb R^3$, componentwise. Complex notation is an encoding of real fields and of real linear equations; the complex object is not itself a physical field, and real parts, imaginary parts and complex conjugation are explicit operations.
object.strategy: State the encoding convention and its regularity: the defining maps are smooth in $(\mathbf x,t)$ because the complex exponential is entire and $(\mathbf x,t)\mapsto\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t$ is linear. No electromagnetic interpretation is asserted; that is a later model choice.

object.title: The electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields
object.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.
object.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: the fields are maps on the product $\Omega\times I$ of the laboratory region with a stated class of regularity, and their fixed-time readings are spatial vector fields in the frame basis. The regularity notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the polar/axial convention and the exclusion of pointwise values at singular source support are conventions recorded explicitly rather than used implicitly. No differential equation and no derived quantity is introduced by this definition.
